noUnboundedLoops.notes: migrate's loop is bounded by caller-supplied maxIterations, clamped to users.length. seedUsers' loop is unbounded in _users.length but is onlyOwner and single-tx gas-bounded (owner chunks the seed themselves). No recursion.

checkedArithmetic.notes: 0.8.19, no unchecked blocks, no assembly beyond the raw call in _tryTransfer. Balance-delta subtractions at L192-196 are safe: the after-balance provably >= before-balance for each token in the bracket.

initializerProtected.notes: Non-upgradeable, constructor-initialized, all four dependency addresses immutable and zero-checked.

pauseMechanism.notes: None. The migrator has no pause of its own; it inherits liveness from V2's and V3's pause states (see LOCAL-103).

inboundCallbackSurface.notes: No ERC721/1155 hooks. Only inbound surface is a transfer hook in phUSD/rewardToken/promoToken firing on the _forward legs; migrate is nonReentrant.

variables.seeded: bool — true once seedUsers has been called at least once. Never reset.
variables.migrateIterator: int256 — 0..users.length during a pass, then -1 on completion. The -1 sentinel mirrors MigratorV1V2's idiom.
variables.users: address[] — replaced wholesale on reseed (delete + push loop). Not deduplicated.
variables.unclaimable: mapping(token => mapping(user => uint256)) — NEW in story-025. Never reset by reseed or by withdrawAll.

transitions.notes: THE STRAGGLER SECOND PASS. Reseed is permitted ONLY between passes — the L126 guard `!seeded || migrateIterator == -1` forbids mid-pass reseed.

chunkingProperties: Cursor advance is monotone and all-or-nothing per chunk: migrate writes migrateIterator ONCE at L209-213 after the loop. A revert anywhere in the loop reverts the whole chunk and the cursor does not move.

Skip-on-zero (L173): a user whose LIVE V2 amount is 0 (exited, or already migrated) is passed over and the cursor still advances. Correct and idempotent — a duplicated address in `users` is a no-op on the second visit.
Coverage is contiguous: end = min(i + maxIterations, len), i starts at the stored cursor.
Live-read design (L172) means no seeded amounts to go stale, and withdrawAll deliberately does NOT abort the pass (unlike MigratorV1V2) — there are no balance preconditions to break.
cursorStateMachine.criticalGap: The all-or-nothing chunk semantics is the migrator's central fragility: ANY revert at index i pins the cursor at i forever, because the L126 reseed guard forbids skipping past it mid-pass. Story-025 removed the reverting FORWARDING legs but left two reverting legs INSIDE the loop (L182 and L188). See LOCAL-101 / LOCAL-102.

perUserHappyPath: 2. Bracket: snapshot phUSDBefore / stableBefore / promoBefore of THIS contract.
3. phlimboV2.withdraw(amount, user) — V2's migrator routing sends principal + auto-claimed stable + freshly minted phUSD rewards to THIS contract (msg.sender).

4. phlimboV3.stake(amount, user) — pulls the principal back out of this contract via safeTransferFrom (max-approved at L156); credits `user`; sets promoDebt against the CURRENT accPromoPerShare so there is no retroactive promo accrual.
5. Deltas: phUSD delta = (principal_in + V2 phUSD rewards + [2nd pass] V3 phUSD auto-claim) - principal_out = exactly the reward component. Principal nets out by construction.
6. _forward each non-zero delta to `user`; on transfer failure bank into unclaimable[token][user] and emit RewardForwardFailed.
valueFlowPaths.bracketArithmeticVerdict: SOUND. The bracket is per-user and symmetric, so pre-existing contract balances (including previously-banked `unclaimable` amounts from earlier iterations, and any donated dust) appear in BOTH before and after and cancel exactly. No cross-user contamination of the delta. Confirmed for all three legs.

strandOrDoubleCountPaths.outcome: STRAND — withdrawAll (L243) sweeps the ENTIRE balance including banked amounts, and does NOT zero the unclaimable entries. Documented as an accepted trade-off in the NatSpec, BUT the stale non-zero entries are beyond what is documented. See LOCAL-105.

strandOrDoubleCountPaths.path: unclaimable banked, contract later re-funded (e.g. to resume migration)
strandOrDoubleCountPaths.outcome: DOUBLE-COUNT — post-sweep, unclaimable entries survive as unbacked claims. Any later inflow makes them first-come-first-served against funds earmarked for other users' forwards. See LOCAL-105.
STRAND (whole pass) — cursor pinned, reseed forbidden mid-pass, no in-contract skip. See LOCAL-101/102.
STRAND (whole pass) — the 'never reverts' guarantee of _forward is not absolute. See LOCAL-104.

strandOrDoubleCountPaths.path: user re-stakes into V2 AFTER their index was processed
strandOrDoubleCountPaths.outcome: NOT stranded — remains in V2, handled by the operational straggler second pass (wind V2 down, reseed, re-run). Documented and correct.
NOT double-counted — live-read returns 0 on the second visit and the iteration is skipped.

strandOrDoubleCountPaths.path: V3 auto-claim on a straggler second pass
strandOrDoubleCountPaths.outcome: NOT stranded — the bracket spans the V3 stake, so V3's auto-claimed rewards (which route to msg.sender == this migrator) are captured in the deltas and forwarded. This is the specific reason the bracket wraps the stake and not just the withdraw. Verified correct.

strandOrDoubleCountPaths.path: standing max phUSD approval to V3 (L156)
strandOrDoubleCountPaths.outcome: NOT exploitable — V3 can only pull via safeTransferFrom where this contract is msg.sender, i.e. only inside phlimboV3.stake called by this contract. V3 is trusted. Noted as a permanent approval surface only.

localFindings.description: phlimboV2.withdraw(amount, user) at L182 is unskippable (no try/catch) and can revert for a user whose V2 position is BRICKED. PhlimboV2.pauseWithdraw (V2 L280-290) reduces user.amount and totalStaked but — unlike PhlimboV3's version — does NOT realign phUSDDebt/stableDebt. A V2 user who partially pauseWithdrew during any V2 pause therefore has debts computed against the old, larger amount, so V2._claimRewards' `userDetails.amount * accPhUSDPerShare / PRECISION - userDetails.phUSDDebt` (V2 L~500) underflows and reverts. V2.withdraw calls _claimRewards unconditionally (V2 L373). PhlimboV3's OWN NatSpec (V3 L521-525) documents this exact defect as 'the latent V1/V2 partial-pauseWithdraw brick' that V3 was written to fix — so the existence of bricked V2 positions is confirmed by the codebase itself, not hypothesised.
localFindings.impact: One such user anywhere in the seeded list reverts the whole chunk, pins migrateIterator at their index, and the L126 reseed guard ('Pass in progress') makes the in-contract skip unreachable. This is the SAME root-cause class and the SAME end state as ledger V3-M-01 ('a single bad recipient bricks the pass, no in-contract recovery'), simply relocated from the forwarding leg to the withdraw leg. Story-025 hardened only the forwarding leg.
localFindings.recommendation: Wrap the per-user body (V2 withdraw + V3 stake + forwards) in try/catch, or add an owner-only `skipIndex`/`setIterator` so a pathological index can be stepped over without a redeploy. Hardening only the transfer legs does not deliver the story's 'the cursor always advances' guarantee.
flags: INCOMPLETE-FIX-CANDIDATE for V3-M-01 — do NOT auto-flip 0b7fa9be... to fixed on the strength of story-025
localFindings.deferTo: code-scanner (confirm the V2 underflow reachability), poc-generator (V2 pause -> partial pauseWithdraw -> V2 unpause -> migrate reverts)

localFindings.description: phlimboV3.stake(amount, user) at L188 is unskippable and reverts with 'Below minimum stake' whenever the LIVE V2 amount is in (0, MINIMUM_STAKE=1e15). V2's ordinary withdraw has a dust rule that forces a full exit rather than leaving sub-minimum dust, and V2.stake requires >= MINIMUM_STAKE — BUT V2.pauseWithdraw (V2 L280-290) has NO dust rule and no minimum, so a partial pauseWithdraw during a V2 pause can leave any dust amount, including 1 wei. migrate's own skip-on-zero guard (L173) only catches amount == 0, not sub-minimum dust.
localFindings.impact: Identical to LOCAL-101: cursor pinned at that index, reseed forbidden mid-pass, recovery is a redeploy + re-wire of both setMigrator roles. A user can self-inflict this cheaply and unilaterally (1 wei of residual stake), so it is also a griefing vector against the migration, not only an accident.
localFindings.recommendation: Change the skip guard to `if (amount < phlimboV3.MINIMUM_STAKE()) continue;` (and handle the dust position out-of-band), or adopt the try/catch from LOCAL-101 which covers both legs at once.
localFindings.deferTo: poc-generator (V2 pause -> pauseWithdraw(amount-1) -> V2 unpause -> migrate reverts 'Below minimum stake')

localFindings.description: migrate requires BOTH V2 and V3 to be unpaused: phlimboV2.withdraw and phlimboV3.stake are each whenNotPaused. Consequently (a) a V3 promo flush (which pauses V3 via beginFlush) halts migration entirely for its duration, and (b) V2 cannot be paused to freeze the user base during migration — the header NatSpec (L22-24) acknowledges this and it is the stated reason for the live-read design. Cursor is not corrupted, only stalled; recorded so the interaction scanner does not mistake the stall for a strand.
localFindings.recommendation: Operational only: do not run a V3 promo rotation concurrently with a migration pass.

localFindings.description: story-025 cloned PhlimboV3._tryTransfer verbatim, including the unchecked `abi.decode(returndata,(bool))`. A token whose transfer SUCCEEDS but returns non-empty return-data shorter than 32 bytes reverts inside the decode; the revert propagates through _forward and out of migrate, pinning the cursor. This directly contradicts _forward's documented 'never reverts' contract (L281-283) and the story-025 commit message's 'so the cursor always advances'. The `callSuccess &&` short-circuit correctly handles the ordinary revert case, so only the success-with-short-returndata case is affected.
localFindings.impact: Token-assumption-gated. phUSD and rewardToken are fixed and vetted; promoToken is owner-vetted per promotion. Low.
localFindings.recommendation: Add `returndata.length >= 32` to the decode guard, in BOTH contracts.
flags: NEW INSTANCE of the V3-L-02 / V3-F-02 root cause in a SECOND contract at this commit — deduplicator MUST NOT silently collapse this into V3-L-02 (different contract, different fingerprint, and the V3 entries do not cover the migrator's cursor-pinning impact).

localFindings.description: withdrawAll sweeps the contract's entire phUSD/rewardToken/promoToken balances INCLUDING amounts banked in `unclaimable`, but does not zero the corresponding entries. The NatSpec (L62-68) explicitly accepts that banked CLAIMS become unbacked and that reimbursement is an out-of-band owner obligation — that trade-off is documented and, under Law 3, not itself reportable. What is NOT covered by the documented trade-off is the residual stale state: (a) the entries persist across a reseed into the next pass (`unclaimable` is never reset by seedUsers), and (b) if the contract is subsequently re-funded — which is expected, since withdrawAll deliberately does NOT abort the pass and migration is meant to resume — the surviving entries become first-come-first-served claims against inflows earmarked for other users' forwards, letting a claimUnclaimable front-run a live migrate chunk's forwarding balance.
localFindings.impact: Requires the owner to have used the last-ditch hatch and then resumed. No theft from an honest counterparty in the normal flow; the migrator holds no value at rest between chunks. Low, footgun-shaped (Law 3: a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised that resuming after a sweep re-arms stale claims).
localFindings.recommendation: Either zero the swept entries (requires tracking banked users/tokens, e.g. a per-token total), or document that withdrawAll is terminal and add an explicit `abortPass`. The current 'sweeps everything but resumption is still supported' combination is the source of the hazard.
localFindings.deferTo: econ-scanner (is the re-fund-and-resume flow actually operationally expected?), severity-classifier

localFindings.description: story-025 rewrote the recovery-note NatSpec to drop the unreachable 'exclude from seed list' escape (addressing ledger V3-F-01). The replacement text now claims 'the cursor always advances and a single bad recipient can never brick a pass'. That claim is true for the forwarding legs and false for the withdraw/stake legs (LOCAL-101/102) and for the decode gap (LOCAL-104). V3-F-01's root complaint — the contract documents recoverability it does not have — therefore SURVIVES story-025 in a new form: the old text overstated an escape hatch, the new text overstates the brick-proofing.

Verified complete: the promo leg mirrors migrate's live read of phlimboV3.promoToken() with the same address(0) handling.

localFindings.description: seedUsers does not reject address(0) or duplicate entries in _users. Both are benign in practice: the live read of userInfo(address(0)) returns amount 0 and is skipped, and duplicates are skipped on the second visit. Owner-supplied input (Law 3: obvious misuse). Recorded for completeness only; not recommended for report.

externalEntryPoints.notes: Does NOT reset `unclaimable`. The between-passes-only guard is what makes LOCAL-101/102 unrecoverable in-contract.

externalCalls: phUSD/rewardToken/promoToken.transfer via _tryTransfer [raw call, non-reverting except LOCAL-104]
externalEntryPoints.notes: Permissionless by design — recipients and amounts are fixed by V2/V3 state, so a third party cannot redirect value. maxIterations is the only caller-controlled input and only bounds gas.

CEI-correct: entry zeroed BEFORE the transfer. Deliberately REVERTING (safeTransfer) — a still-blocked caller reverts and keeps their claim, which is the right semantics on a user-initiated path. `token` is caller-supplied but only indexes the caller's own banked balance, so an arbitrary-token argument cannot mint a claim.

stateChanges: none — balances only; notably does NOT touch users/migrateIterator/unclaimable
externalEntryPoints.notes: Last-ditch hatch. Deliberately does NOT abort the pass (live reads mean no balance preconditions). See LOCAL-105.

externalEntryPoints.function: unclaimable(address,address) / users(uint256) / seeded() / migrateIterator() / phlimboV2() / phlimboV3() / phUSD() / rewardToken()

externalCalls.notes: REQUIRES wiring prerequisite (a): phlimboV2.setMigrator(this). Without it, withdraw reverts 'Not authorized' and the pass cannot start at all (fail-loud, not a strand). withdraw is whenNotPaused and CAN revert on bricked positions — see LOCAL-101.
REQUIRES wiring prerequisite (b): phlimboV3.setMigrator(this). stake is whenNotPaused and enforces MINIMUM_STAKE — see LOCAL-102/103. Holds a standing max phUSD approval (L156).
No mint role needed on this contract — V2 mints the pending phUSD rewards during its withdraw.
Assumed standard ERC20, no fee-on-transfer, no hooks.

externalCalls.target: IERC20 promoToken (LIVE-read from V3 each call)
externalCalls.notes: Read once per migrate/withdrawAll call, so it cannot shift mid-loop. V3 guarantees promoToken is never phUSD or rewardToken, which is what makes the three balance brackets independent — this guarantee is LOAD-BEARING for the delta arithmetic and is worth an explicit cross-contract assertion.

A user with a token-transfer callback gets control inside migrate's loop; migrate is nonReentrant so re-entry into migrate/claimUnclaimable is blocked. Re-entry into V2/V3 from that callback is possible (they have their own guards) — surfaced for the interaction scanner, not adjudicated here.

stateVariables.name: users
stateVariables.notes: Not deduplicated, not zero-checked (LOCAL-108); both benign via skip-on-zero.

stateVariables.name: migrateIterator
stateVariables.notes: int256 with a -1 completion sentinel, mirroring MigratorV1V2. Written once per migrate call, after the loop — so a revert leaves it untouched (the pinning mechanism in LOCAL-101/102).

stateVariables.name: unclaimable
stateVariables.notes: NEW in story-025. NOT reset by seedUsers and NOT reduced by withdrawAll — the source of LOCAL-105. Per-user granularity here is strictly better than PhlimboV3's aggregate unclaimablePromo, which has no per-user record at all.

trustAssumptions: Both wiring prerequisites are performed by the staging scripts before migrate: phlimboV2.setMigrator(this) and phlimboV3.setMigrator(this). Neither is asserted in-contract; absence fails loud ('Not authorized'), not silently.
The migrator role is REVOKED on both V2 and V3 once migration completes — while wired, this contract can withdraw any V2 user's stake to itself. Not asserted or self-revoked in-contract.
V3 guarantees promoToken is never phUSD or rewardToken (enforced in startPromotion). LOAD-BEARING for the three independent balance brackets in migrate.
phUSD, rewardToken and promoToken are standard ERC20s with no transfer hooks and no fee-on-transfer; a fee-on-transfer token would make the L192-196 deltas under-report but would not underflow.

The owner is non-malicious (Law 3): withdrawAll's unconditional sweep and the seeded list's contents are trusted inputs and are not reported as attack vectors. LOCAL-105 is scoped to the non-obvious footgun (resume-after-sweep re-arms stale claims), not to the sweep itself.
Operationally, V2 is wound down (APY -> 0, collectReward stopped) before the straggler second pass — otherwise stragglers regenerate indefinitely. Documented at L40-44; not enforceable in-contract.
handoffToInteractionAnalysis: PRIORITY: LOCAL-101 and LOCAL-102 are the headline. Both are INCOMPLETE-FIX candidates against ledger V3-M-01 (fix-pending, 0b7fa9be...). story-025 hardened the forwarding legs only; the withdraw and stake legs inside the same loop remain unskippable and revert-capable, reproducing M-01's exact end state (pinned cursor, no in-contract recovery, redeploy-only). Per CLAUDE.md an incomplete fix outranks an unfixed bug — do NOT propose V3-M-01 fixed.

The trigger for both is PhlimboV2.pauseWithdraw's missing debt realignment and missing dust rule — a V2 defect that PhlimboV3 explicitly fixed in its own pauseWithdraw (V3 L521-525) and that the migrator then walks straight into. Root cause is in V2 (deployed, out of scope for change), impact is in MigratorV2V3 (in scope, fixable) — file against the migrator.
PROPOSE FIXED: V3-Q-01 (promo sweep, LOCAL-107). Human applies.
DEDUP INSTRUCTION: LOCAL-104 is a NEW instance of the V3-L-02/F-02 abi.decode root cause in a second contract with a distinct impact (cursor pinning vs flush bricking). Do not collapse.

TREAT AS AXIOM: the per-user balance-delta bracket is arithmetically sound and free of cross-user contamination; the principal nets out exactly. Any finding premised on the migrator mis-computing a reward delta from prior balances is REFUTED.
TREAT AS AXIOM: skip-on-zero + live reads make migrate idempotent per user; duplicates and post-processing V2 re-stakes cannot double-credit.
